title: Scan the full codebase for bespoke platform, path, env, and repo/workspace handling that should use existing shared modules
scope: Cross-cutting H31 scan across src/**, tools/**, bin/**, tests/**, extensions/**, sublime/**, and benchmark query metadata for bespoke platform/path/env/repo-workspace handling that should converge on existing shared modules.

summary.overallAssessment: The codebase already has the right shared primitives for several cross-cutting concerns, but adoption is uneven. The strongest current shared anchors are src/shared/direct-execution.js, src/shared/subprocess/windows-cmd.js, src/shared/runtime-envelope.js, src/shared/dispatch/env.js, src/shared/indexing/build-pointer.js, src/shared/files.js, and the workspace config/manifest surfaces. The main remaining cleanup is not inventing new abstractions first; it is replacing bespoke call-site logic with those existing modules, especially in CLI entrypoint guards, Windows wrapper handling, runtime env propagation, and build-root/repo/workspace resolution seams.

highestPriorityHotspots.whyItMatters: Symlink-unsafe direct execution guards can silently skip CLI behavior when entrypoints are launched through shims or symlinked wrappers.
Wrapper resolution, PATH probing, cmd.exe fallback, and runtime env shaping are correctness-sensitive on Windows and currently duplicated across tooling and editor surfaces.
Local repo/workspace/build-root resolution logic risks drifting from the current generation/build pointer contract and from API allowlist behavior.

hotspotMatrix.name: Symlink-unsafe direct-execution guards
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Migrate exact process.argv[1] versus fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) checks to src/shared/direct-execution.js unless the script intentionally wants basename-based detection for generated wrappers.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: The direct-execution helper already handles symlinked launches safely. Reusing it removes a proven bug class instead of replicating path-comparison logic file by file.
exceptions: tools/ci/run-suite.js already carries a realpath-aware implementation and should either stay as-is or converge carefully without regressing its normalize-for-compare semantics.
tools/bench/graph/store-lazy-load.js and similar basename-based benches should remain local only if they intentionally accept renamed fixture wrappers rather than exact module identity.

hotspotMatrix.name: Windows command wrapper and PATH probing duplication
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Converge wrapper resolution and cmd.exe fallback on src/shared/subprocess/windows-cmd.js, and leave only packaging-specific adapter code local where the extension bundle genuinely requires vendored runtime files.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: This surface already absorbed recent Windows wrapper bugs. Keeping one canonical wrapper policy reduces another class of ENOENT and shell-fallback drift.
exceptions: extensions/vscode/windows-cmd.js and extensions/vscode/windows-cmd-core.cjs must remain physically bundled for the extension package, but they should be treated as a vendored mirror of the shared implementation rather than an independently evolving fork.
tools/package-vscode.js may keep a tiny packaging smoke probe, but not its own long-term wrapper policy.

hotspotMatrix.name: Runtime environment shaping and propagation drift
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Use the shared runtime envelope/env surfaces for env shaping and reserve direct process.env merging for truly local child-process payload injection only.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: Runtime envelope code already centralizes NODE_OPTIONS, UV threadpool, and override precedence. Reusing it prevents configuration drift between bench, service, setup, and CLI surfaces.
exceptions: Extensions and TUI code may still need local env layering for editor/session-specific state, but should feed that through a shared base env rather than rebuilding runtime policy from scratch.
Tests that intentionally mutate process.env for isolation do not need to adopt runtime-envelope helpers unless they are asserting production env behavior.

hotspotMatrix.name: Build-root and generation-resolution duplication
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Eliminate bespoke current-build resolution and route generation/build-root lookups through the shared build-pointer module plus workspace manifest/config helpers.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: The build-pointer surface already embodies the current generation contract. Duplicating resolution logic is exactly how stale or mismatched build-root behavior reappears.
exceptions: Reporting code may keep presentation-specific fallback behavior, but the underlying current-build selection should come from shared build-pointer helpers.

hotspotMatrix.name: Repo/workspace allowlist and identity handling drift
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Keep API and extension-specific UX or trust-boundary decisions local, but centralize repo/workspace identity normalization and manifest/build-root interpretation on shared workspace helpers.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: The API and editor surfaces have legitimate policy differences, but they should not each reinterpret workspace identity, cache roots, or build-pointer payloads independently.
exceptions: tools/api/trust-boundary.js should remain API-local because it owns HTTP trust and allowlist policy, not generic workspace normalization.
extensions/vscode/extension.js should keep workspace-folder selection and repo-walkup UX local, while reusing shared normalization where possible.

hotspotMatrix.name: Path normalization and containment helpers split across surfaces
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Use shared path normalization helpers for common operations and reserve local containment helpers for surface-specific policy boundaries.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: toPosix and shared filesystem helpers are already common. Consolidating normalization reduces subtle casing/relative-path inconsistencies without forcing every boundary check into one over-generalized helper.
exceptions: API and extension containment checks that encode product policy can remain local once they consume canonical normalized inputs.

mappings.problemSurface: Windows wrapper resolution and shell fallback

localExceptions.reasonToRemainLocal: Owns API-specific authz and filesystem-boundary policy; should consume normalized inputs from shared modules but keep HTTP trust semantics local.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainPartlyLocal: Needs editor-session UX, workspace folder selection, and VS Code-specific lifecycle hooks that do not belong in src/shared, even though normalization and wrapper helpers should converge.
Cargo target/output conventions are TUI-packaging specific, but the env and wrapper baseline should still come from shared runtime/platform helpers.
Bench harnesses may intentionally allow basename-style execution from generated wrappers or fixture paths; only exact module-identity checks should migrate wholesale.

recommendedFollowUps.why: Apply the API/runtime/server-side adoption changes identified here.
Apply the tooling/setup/bench-side adoption changes identified here.
Apply the editor/extension/integration adoption changes identified here, especially the VS Code wrapper/env seams.
If workspace/cache-root/build-pointer adoption still feels fragmented after H31, factor a more explicit shared repo/workspace/generation helper family.
If wrapper/runtime envelope adoption still leaves awkward local seams, formalize a broader shared subprocess/toolchain helper family.
